result.title: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops
result.comment: Initial version released to encourage open discussion and share preliminary findings. Evaluations of additional open-source System One models are ongoing
result.summary: System One models choose an agent's next action by scoring a supplied set of options in a single pass. This makes them fast and cheap, but when they choose wrongly there is nothing to inspect: did the model misread what the agent has seen, or read it correctly and still act wrongly? We answer behaviorally. On a frozen benchmark of agent decision states from simulated environments, customer-service policies, tool use, web navigation and coding, we pair every next-action question with factual probes about the same state, each answered independently. Across seventeen fast systems and a reasoning model, the answer is consistent: most wrong actions follow correct reading, and the more accurate a system, the more of its errors take this form. These errors are not noise; they gather on the same states across systems of every kind. Where the probed facts provably determine the action, models that read every fact still fail to combine them, and their own answers, composed by code, repair the failure. On real states, what is missing is often not a fact but the next sub-goal.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在涵盖模拟环境、客服策略、工具使用、网页导航与编码的冻结 agent 决策状态基准上，为每个「下一步动作」问题配上同一状态的事实探针并独立作答，从而行为性地区分模型是「误读状态」还是「读对却行动错误」；在十七个 System One 快速系统与一个推理模型上发现多数错误源于正确读取后的组合失败，且错误跨系统聚集在同一状态上，缺失的往往是下一个子目标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「读对但用错」的诊断框架与 LVR 关心的 latent 内容是否真正被答案使用、信息坍缩和视觉旁路问题直接相关，事实探针与代码组合修复的做法可供核查推理状态中证据保留与贡献分配的成因。
